title: How to Know When an AI Agent Can Work Unsupervised — Evan Kormos, Coinbase
talk_summary: Coinbase's Evan Kormos argues for modeling agent workflows as policy-bounded DAGs with adaptive inner loops, where each node's check is backed by evals/traces and autonomy is earned through supervised-to-sampled rollout. The practical core is deterministic outer control, measurable quality gates, and human fallback/exception handling.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic outer DAG, adaptive inner loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Represent the workflow as explicit gated steps and let agents iterate only inside a node until its check passes, with bounded retries and exception paths.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep it deterministic on the outside and make it adaptive on the inside.

takeaways.technique: Calibrate the check with repeated evals and traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Define good with representative data, run repeated evaluations, and use traces to measure whether the gate actually catches defects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The loop is really only as trustworthy as the check.

takeaways.what_they_do: Start with full human verification, move to sampling when measured confidence clears a policy threshold, then humans handle exceptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When measured confidence reaches a policy threshold, we can move towards sampling.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run independent reviews alongside each other, combine results, and still keep required checks in place.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run independent reviews alongside each other, bring the results together, but keep the required checks in place.

takeaways.technique: Inject workflow state into agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Tell the agent where it sits in the DAG, what upstream/downstream gates matter, and the longer-horizon goal instead of dumping raw history.
takeaways.evidence_quote: inject the DAG state into our agent and let it know kind of where it fits

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument process metrics because parallel agents shift volume and create new bottlenecks; visibility matters more than workflow authoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the operational visibility of the process is extremely important much more important than the authoring and the building of your workflow tool.
